```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.94, out.width = "100%")
library(manimR)
manim_config(verbosity = "WARNING", progress_bar = FALSE)
in_pkgdown <- identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(format = if (in_pkgdown) "auto" else "png", quality = "l")
manim_config(media_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "manimR-media"))
has_survival <- requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)
```

Why does a survival curve stay flat when someone leaves follow-up? This
article answers with one scene built from a `survival::survfit()` result.
Six people are followed. At each event the curve drops by the share of the
people still at risk who had the event; a censored person leaves the risk
set without moving the curve.

The scene uses three things from manimR:

* `keyed_mobjects()` and `update_keyed()`, so each person keeps their own
  dot from the first frame to the last and leaves when they stop being at
  risk;
* `Axes$plot_step()` and `Axes$plot_band()`, which draw the estimate and
  its confidence band as step functions;
* `Text()` labels, so the scene needs no LaTeX.

## The data and the estimate

```{r data, eval = has_survival}
people <- data.frame(id = LETTERS[1:6], time = c(2, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7), status = c(1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0))
fit <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ 1, data = people)
km <- data.frame(time = fit$time, at_risk = fit$n.risk, events = fit$n.event, surv = fit$surv,
                 lower = fit$lower, upper = fit$upper)
km
```

The scene draws the numbers in `km`; it computes nothing itself. Before an
event at time `t` the risk set is everyone whose time is at least `t`, and
the estimate after `t` is the estimate before it times
`1 - events / at_risk`. Both match `survfit()`:

```{r check, eval = has_survival}
stopifnot(
  all.equal(km$at_risk, vapply(km$time, function(t) sum(people$time >= t), 0)),
  all.equal(km$surv, cumprod(1 - km$events / km$at_risk))
)
```

## The scene

The people sit in a row above the axes. At each time in `km` the people who
leave (an event or censoring) are highlighted while they still count in the
denominator, the curve steps to its new value, and then they fade out of the
risk set.

```{manim kaplan-meier, eval = has_survival}
KaplanMeier <- manim_scene(function(self) {
  ax <- Axes(x_range = c(0, 8, 1), y_range = c(0, 1, 0.25), x_length = 9, y_length = 4.2, tips = FALSE,
             axis_config = list(include_numbers = FALSE))$shift(DOWN * 0.9)
  x_labels <- VGroup(lapply(0:8, function(x) Text(as.character(x), font_size = 20)$next_to(ax$c2p(x, 0), DOWN)))
  y_labels <- VGroup(lapply(c(0, 0.5, 1), function(y) Text(format(y), font_size = 20)$next_to(ax$c2p(0, y), LEFT)))
  person <- function(r) {
    x <- -3.75 + 1.5 * (match(r$id, people$id) - 1)
    VGroup(Dot(c(x, 2.9, 0), radius = 0.18, color = BLUE), Text(r$id, font_size = 22)$move_to(c(x, 3.35, 0)))
  }
  at_risk <- keyed_mobjects(people, "id", person)
  counter <- Text(sprintf("At risk: %d", nrow(people)), font_size = 26)$to_corner(UR)
  estimate <- Text("S(t) = 1", font_size = 26)$next_to(counter, DOWN)$align_to(counter, RIGHT)
  self$add(ax, x_labels, y_labels, at_risk, counter, estimate)
  curve <- ax$plot_step(0, 1, x_end = 0.01, color = YELLOW)
  self$add(curve)
  surv <- 1
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(km))) {
    t <- km$time[i]
    leaving <- people$id[people$time == t]
    ids <- people$id[people$time > t]
    # Highlight who leaves while they still count in the denominator.
    self$play(lapply(leaving, function(k) at_risk[[k]]$animate$set_color(if (people$status[people$id == k] == 1) RED else GREY)),
              Transform(counter, Text(sprintf("At risk: %d", km$at_risk[i]), font_size = 26)$move_to(counter)),
              run_time = 0.6)
    surv <- km$surv[i]
    new_curve <- ax$plot_step(c(0, km$time[seq_len(i)]), c(1, km$surv[seq_len(i)]), x_end = t + 0.01, color = YELLOW)
    label <- if (km$events[i] > 0) sprintf("S(t) = %.3f", surv) else sprintf("S(t) = %.3f (censored, no step)", surv)
    self$play(Transform(curve, new_curve),
              Transform(estimate, Text(label, font_size = 26)$next_to(counter, DOWN)$align_to(counter, RIGHT)),
              run_time = 0.8)
    self$play(update_keyed(at_risk, people[people$id %in% ids, ]), run_time = 0.6)
  }
  final <- ax$plot_step(c(0, km$time), c(1, km$surv), x_end = 8, color = YELLOW)
  band <- ax$plot_band(c(0, km$time), c(1, km$lower), c(1, km$upper), color = YELLOW, opacity = 0.2, step = TRUE)
  self$play(Transform(curve, final), FadeIn(band), run_time = 1)
  self$wait(1)
})
```

The last frame shows the full estimate with its 95% confidence band from
`survfit()` (the default log scale, whose upper limit is 1 here).

## Stills and a lesson from the same scene

The same scene gives the frames for a handout. `storyboard()` runs it once
and draws the chosen times side by side as vectors:

```{r storyboard, eval = FALSE}
storyboard(KaplanMeier, t = c("Day 2 event" = 1.2, "Day 4 event" = 3.2, "End" = Inf),
           "kaplan-meier.pdf")
```

`write_lesson()` turns a render into a folder that plays offline, with a
chapter for each section of the scene and the captions added with
`add_subcaption()`:

```{r lesson, eval = FALSE}
out <- render(KaplanMeier, quality = "m")
write_lesson(out, "kaplan-meier-lesson", title = "Kaplan-Meier, step by step")
```
